recovery_analysis.thesis: Jubilee (<$12/boe lifting cost) & TEN fields + GTA FLNG Phase 1 startup (2.5 mtpa); multi-year FCF inflection.

annotations.note: Extended $1.2bn RBL to Apr-2033; 9M26 EBITDAX ~$800m, capex $281m, net debt cut >$500m YTD to $2.47bn, cash $103.75m.
100% of crude/refined product export proceeds flow directly into offshore collection accounts; debt service for international Eurobonds is deducted prior to any fiscal repatriation.
Low cash lifting cost ($8 - $18/boe) ensures robust operating profitability and positive cash flow even during severe oil price downturns ($50/bbl).
Proved plus probable commercial reserves provide a durable 12-18 year production life, underpinning long-dated senior paper.
9M26 EBITDAX ~$800m (~2x YoY); net debt slashed >$500m YTD to $2.47bn (target <$2.4bn YE26).

verdict.stance: Overweight / Rapid Deleveraging ($500m+ Debt Cut YTD) & Doubled 9M EBITDAX ($800m)
verdict.summary: Sharp credit turnaround in 2026: 9M26 EBITDAX nearly doubled YoY to ~$800m on rising production and lower opex, enabling Kosmos to slash net debt by >$500m YTD to $2.47bn (from $2.98bn at start of 2026), with management targeting <$2.4bn by YE26.

positives: Aggressive deleveraging: cut net debt >$500m YTD to $2.47bn (target <$2.4bn YE26).
9M26 EBITDAX nearly doubled YoY to ~$800m as Tortue FLNG & Jubilee/Winterfell ramp.
Multi-basin diversification across Ghana, Gulf of Mexico, Equatorial Guinea, and Mauritania/Senegal.
negatives: Still elevated gross debt (~$2.5bn+ RBL + senior notes) and B-/B3 ratings.
Brent crude price sensitivity and Tortue FLNG operational ramp execution.
